subject: Theory of Automata and Formal Languages
verificationNote: Worked against AKTU paper ID 411411. DFA/NFA diagram transitions were transcribed by inspecting page images; graph interpretation should be independently reviewed. PDA q6b accepts singleton aaaa under conventional empty-stack acceptance; paper omits final-state acceptance specification. Answers are instructor-review-pending.

questions.question: Define DFA formally and compare NFA.
questions.answer: DFA is a five-tuple M=(Q,Σ,δ,q0,F): finite states Q, input alphabet Σ, total transition function δ:Q×Σ→Q, initial state q0∈Q, accepting set F⊆Q. For each state/symbol DFA has exactly one next state and no ε transitions. NFA transition δ:Q×Σ→P(Q) (ε-NFA includes ε), permitting several/zero alternatives. NFA accepts if at least one computation ends in accepting state. Both recognize exactly regular languages; subset construction transforms NFA to DFA, potentially using up to 2^|Q| states.

questions.question: Construct DFA accepting binary strings ending in 101.
questions.answer: Track longest suffix that is a prefix of 101: q0 none, q1 '1', q2 '10', q3 '101' accept. Transitions (on 0,1): q0→(q0,q1); q1→(q2,q1); q2→(q0,q3); q3→(q2,q1). Start q0, accept {q3}. Examples accepted: 101,0101,1101; rejected 10,1010,111.

questions.question: Regular expression for binary strings containing consecutive 00 and consecutive 11.
questions.answer: Let Σ=(0|1). Required substrings '00' and '11' may appear in either order; a correct regex is Σ*00Σ*11Σ* | Σ*11Σ*00Σ*. It accepts 0011,1100,001011 and rejects 0000 (no 11) or 1111 (no 00). Parentheses around alternatives make precedence unambiguous.

questions.question: Find language generated by S→SS|ab|ba|ε.
questions.answer: Base words are ab, ba and ε. Rule S→SS concatenates words from the language, so L=(ab|ba)*, including ε, ab, ba, abab, abba, baab, baba etc. Every nonempty generated word has even length and can be partitioned into adjacent blocks each equal to ab or ba; not every equal-count a/b word is generated (e.g. aabb is excluded).

questions.question: Leftmost derivation for 00110101 in grammar S→0B|1A, A→0|0S|1AA, B→1|1S|0BB.
questions.answer: One valid leftmost derivation (replace leftmost nonterminal each step): S⇒0B⇒00BB⇒001B⇒0011S⇒00110B⇒001101S⇒0011010B⇒00110101. The choices: S→0B, B→0BB, left B→1, B→1S, S→0B, B→1S, S→0B, B→1. Final word exactly 00110101.

questions.question: Two-stack PDA and language it accepts beyond a one-stack PDA.
questions.answer: A two-stack PDA has finite control and two independent pushdown stacks. It can simulate a Turing machine by storing symbols to the left/right of the simulated tape head on different stacks, and is thus Turing-powerful (with suitable acceptance conventions), strictly beyond one-stack PDA which recognizes context-free languages. Example L={a^n b^n c^n | n≥1} is not context-free, so no ordinary one-stack PDA accepts it, whereas a two-stack PDA can count a's, match b's and then c's using the two stacks.

questions.question: Explain multitape Turing machine.
questions.answer: A k-tape TM has k independently addressable tapes, each with read/write head. Transition δ:Q×Γ^k→Q×Γ^k×{L,R,S}^k simultaneously reads k symbols, writes k symbols and moves each head. It may copy input to work tapes, sort/search more easily and run faster in practice. A single-tape TM simulates it by encoding all tapes and head positions, so multitape adds convenience/efficiency but not computability; recognizable/decidable languages are unchanged.

questions.question: DFA accepting binary numerals divisible by 4.
questions.answer: Use states for remainder mod4, plus fresh start s rejecting empty string: r0,r1,r2,r3 represent numeric value modulo4, r0 is only accepting state. δ(s,0)=r0, δ(s,1)=r1. For each remainder r and bit b∈{0,1}, δ(r,b)=r_( (2r+b) mod4 ). Thus table 0→r0/r1, 1→r2/r3, 2→r0/r1, 3→r2/r3 (on 0/1). Starting s, '0','100','1100' accept; '1','10','101' reject. Leading zeros are allowed. This is a correct DFA even if not state-minimal.

questions.question: Regular expression using Arden's theorem for the printed three-state DFA.
questions.answer: From the diagram: start q0 is accepting, q1 also accepting, q2 nonaccepting. Transitions q0:0→q1,1→q2; q1:0→q1,1→q2; q2:0→q0,1→q2. Equivalent language is ε plus all nonempty binary strings whose last symbol is 0. Regular expression: ε | (0|1)*0. By Arden's lemma, if R=Q R | P and ε∉Q, then R=Q* P. q0 and q1 are behaviorally equivalent (both accepting, 0 to accepting, 1 to rejecting), and q2 is rejecting until a 0 arrives. Minimal equivalent automaton has two states: accepting A (start), rejecting B; A:0→A,1→B; B:0→A,1→B.

questions.question: Construct equivalent left-linear grammar from right-linear S→0A|1B; A→0C|1A|0; B→1B|1A|1; C→0|0A.
questions.answer:
Convert given grammar to NFA with states S,A,B,C and final F: every production X→aY gives edge X -a-> Y; X→a gives edge X -a-> F. Reverse NFA edges into left-linear productions (Y→X a), take F as grammar start and S→ε as terminal finish. One equivalent left-linear grammar with start F:
F→A0 | B1 | C0
A→S0 | A1 | B1 | C0
B→S1 | B1
C→A0
S→ε.
This grammar is left-linear because any nonterminal precedes the final terminal in each nonempty RHS. Verify example original S⇒0A⇒00 (via A→0) is generated by new grammar F⇒A0⇒S00⇒00; original S⇒1B⇒11 becomes F⇒B1⇒S11⇒11.

questions.question: DPDA vs NPDA and PDA for L={a^n b^n | n≥1}.
questions.answer: DPDA has at most one enabled transition for a state/input/top combination and cannot mix an ε-move with an input-consuming move for the same configuration; recognizes deterministic context-free languages. NPDA can branch and recognizes all context-free languages. For L, use a DPDA (with end marker $ to ensure stopping): states q_push,q_pop,q_accept, stack bottom Z and count symbol A. On 'a' in q_push, push A; on first 'b' switch to q_pop and pop A; on 'b' in q_pop pop A; on '$' in q_pop with top Z go q_accept. Other transitions undefined/reject. Require at least one 'a' and at least one 'b' by requiring first b to enter q_pop. E.g. aabb: push2, pop2, '$' accept; aab rejects.

questions.question: DTM vs NDTM; design TM deciding L={ww | w∈{a,b}*}.
questions.answer: Deterministic TM δ maps each state/symbol to at most one action; nondeterministic TM permits a set of actions/branches and accepts if some branch accepts. Both recognize same recursively enumerable languages and decide same recursive languages (with potentially different running times). L={ww} is decidable though not context-free. A practical multitape TM design: 1) scan input and count length n in binary; reject odd n; 2) copy first n/2 symbols to tape2 (one-symbol alphabet a/b); 3) reset tape2 head and scan the remaining n/2 symbols on input tape1 in lockstep, rejecting at the first mismatch; 4) accept iff all comparisons match and input ends. Such a multitape design can be simulated by an ordinary single-tape TM; a nondeterministic approach may guess the midpoint but must verify exact equal-length halves and equal symbols.

questions.question: Convert printed ε-NFA with states 1,2,3,4 to DFA.
questions.answer: Read diagram transitions: 1 --0→2, 1 --ε→3; 3 --ε→2, 3 --0→4; 2 --1→2 (self-loop), 2 --1→4; 4 --0→3. Initial state 1; accepting states 3 and 4. ε-closures E(1)={1,3,2}, E(2)={2}, E(3)={3,2}, E(4)={4}. Subset construction yields states A={1,2,3} start/accept, B={2,4} accept, C={2,3} accept, D={4} accept, and dead Ø. Transitions (on 0,1): A→(B,B); B→(C,B); C→(D,B); D→(C,Ø); Ø→(Ø,Ø). Accept each subset containing 3 or 4. All these are reachable from A; note the original ε-NFA accepts ε because ε path 1→3 reaches final state.

questions.question: Minimize printed DFA with q0..q6.
questions.answer:
From diagram accepting q5,q6. Transitions q0:(a→q1,b→q2), q1:(a→q2,b→q3), q2:(a→q4,b→q6), q3:(a→q4,b→q5), q4:(a→q3,b→q6), q5:(a→q5,b→q6), q6:(a→q5,b→q6). Partition by acceptance: {q0,q1,q2,q3,q4}, {q5,q6}. Refine: q2,q3,q4 equivalent (a stays among them, b→accepting); q1 differs because b→q3 (nonaccept); q0 differs because a→q1 vs a→{q2,q3,q4}. Final minimal four-state DFA:
A={q0} start: on a→B,on b→C
B={q1}: on a→C,on b→C
C={q2,q3,q4}: on a→C,on b→D
D={q5,q6} accept: on a→D,on b→D.
Only D is accepting. This minimization uses the actual arrows shown in the paper's figure.

questions.question: Pumping lemma for regular languages; prove {a^p | p prime} nonregular.
questions.answer: Pumping lemma: if L regular, there exists pumping length N such that any w∈L with |w|≥N decomposes w=xyz with |xy|≤N, |y|≥1, and xy^i z∈L for all i≥0. Suppose primes-length unary language regular and choose prime p≥N (primes unbounded). For w=a^p, y=a^k where 1≤k≤N. Choose i=p+1; pumped length |xy^(p+1)z|=p+p k=p(k+1), composite because p≥2 and k+1≥2. Contradiction. Therefore L={a^p : p prime} is not regular.

questions.question: Closure properties of regular languages.
questions.answer: If L1,L2 regular then union L1∪L2 is recognized by an ε-NFA branching to both start states (or product DFA). Intersection by product DFA with accept states F1×F2. Complement Σ*\L by swapping final and nonfinal states of a **complete** DFA (same alphabet). Difference L1\L2 = L1∩(Σ*\L2). Concatenation L1L2 by ε-transitions from L1 accepting states to L2 start. Kleene star by new accepting start with ε path to old start and loops from old accepts. Regular languages are also closed under reversal, homomorphism and inverse homomorphism.

questions.question: Transform grammar S→bA|aB, A→bAA|aS|a, B→aBB|bS|b to Chomsky normal form.
questions.answer:
Introduce terminal-symbol variables T_a→a, T_b→b, pair variables X→AA, Y→BB and new start S0 (because original S occurs on RHS). CNF productions:
S0→T_b A | T_a B
S→T_b A | T_a B
A→T_b X | T_a S | a
B→T_a Y | T_b S | b
X→A A
Y→B B
T_a→a
T_b→b.
Every production is X→YZ or X→terminal (except optional S0→ε absent here). The new start S0 never occurs on right side. Equivalent because bAA becomes T_b X and aBB becomes T_a Y without altering generated terminal words.

questions.question: CFG for (i) 0^m1^n with m≠n, m,n≥1; (ii) a^p b^q c^r with p+q=r and p,q≥1.
questions.answer:
(i) Split into m>n or n>m. Grammar:
S→G | H
G→0G1 | 0E1
E→0E | 0
H→0H1 | 0F1
F→1F | 1.
G derives 0^(n+k)1^n with n,k≥1; H derives 0^n1^(n+k) with n,k≥1. Hence positive unequal counts exactly.
(ii) Grammar S→a S c | a B c; B→b B c | b c. Each 'a' and 'b' adds one trailing 'c', so every generated a^p b^q c^(p+q) has p,q≥1 and conversely is generable.

questions.question: Construct PDA equivalent to CFG S→0S1|A, A→1A0|S|ε.
questions.answer: Use standard CFG-to-NPDA conversion accepting by empty stack. Stack top on left, initial stack symbol S; one state q (or add start/accept states). For each production X→α add ε-transition (q,ε,X)→(q,α), with α pushed so its leftmost symbol becomes top; in particular δ(q,ε,S) can replace S by 0S1 or A, and δ(q,ε,A) replace A by 1A0 or S or ε. For each terminal t∈{0,1}, add δ(q,t,t)→(q,ε) (consume matching input). Accept when input exhausted and stack empty. This nondeterministically derives a sentence from grammar, then matches terminals. CFG has unit-cycle S→A→S; nondeterministic infinite branches exist but accepting branches remain correct. Example empty word: S⇒A⇒ε and PDA pops S,A without reading input.

questions.question: Find equivalent CFG of PDA with transitions δ(q0,a,z0)=(q0,az0), δ(q0,a,a)=(q1,aa), δ(q1,a,a)=(q1,ε), δ(q1,ε,z0)=(q1,ε).
questions.answer: Assume standard acceptance by empty stack; no final-state set is supplied. The first input a changes z0→a z0 (one a on stack); the next a in q0 changes a→aa, and moves to q1 (two a stack symbols). Each further a in q1 removes one a; exactly two more a's are required before the ε move removes z0. Thus language is singleton {aaaa}={a^4}. A CFG is S→aaaa (or S→aA, A→aB, B→aC, C→a). If instead acceptance by final state is intended, the printed PDA lacks declared accepting states, so its language cannot be uniquely determined; empty-stack interpretation is the conventional one here.

questions.question: TM for L={a^(2n)b^n|n≥1} and trace aaaabb.
questions.answer: Construct single-tape marking TM using symbols X (consumed a), Y (consumed b), blank. Loop: find leftmost unmarked a and mark X; continue right to next unmarked a and mark X (reject if missing); scan right past remaining a's and marked b's to find next unmarked b, mark Y (reject if missing or if b occurs before all a's); rewind head to left boundary; repeat. When no unmarked a remains, scan remainder to ensure no unmarked b or bad symbols; require ≥1 triple, accept. Trace (head positions omitted, left-to-right tape snapshots): aaaabb→Xaaabb (mark first a)→XXaabb (mark second a)→XXaaYb (mark b)→XXXaYb→XXXXYb→XXXXYY→ACCEPT. Standard q states encode phases find-a1, find-a2, find-b, rewind, check, accept/reject. For n=2, a^4 b^2 is accepted; aaab rejects. Algorithm halts on every finite input.

questions.question: Universal Turing Machine, Post correspondence, recursive versus recursively enumerable.
questions.answer: Universal TM U takes an encoded TM ⟨M⟩ and input w, and simulates M(w), establishing general-purpose stored-program computation. U halts iff simulated M halts (unless U is explicitly bounded). Post Correspondence Problem (PCP) gives finitely many domino tiles (top_i,bottom_i) and asks if a nonempty sequence of tile indices, repetitions allowed, makes concatenated tops equal concatenated bottoms. PCP is undecidable in general. Recursive/decidable languages have a TM halting on all inputs with yes/no answer. Recursively enumerable (RE/Turing-recognizable) languages have a TM that halts and accepts members, but may run forever for nonmembers. Every recursive language is RE, but some RE languages are undecidable (e.g. halting set); complements of both L and its complement RE implies L recursive.
